fields.System.Title: FDN-4 — Audit trail
fields.System.Description:
Purpose

Every write is recorded with who did it, when, and what changed — permanently, and without
slowing down the warehouse.

Scope

In. Automatic audit capture on writes, an audit query endpoint, table partitioning.

Out. Field-level diffing of every record. Log shipping to an external SIEM.

Design notes

Append-only. Audit rows are never updated or deleted. A correction is a new row.

audit_log will be your largest table — roughly one row per API call. By month six a
full-table scan of it can take the database down. FDN-403 partitions by month and moves
partitions older than 90 days to cold storage. This is not optional work.

Do not put audit writes inside the hot business transaction if it measurably slows confirm
endpoints. Measure first — a single insert usually costs nothing, and correctness beats
speculation.

Risks

| Risk | Reference |
|---|---|
| Audit table growth degrades the whole database | [doc 04 §3.1](../../../docs/04-modules.md) |
| Audit writes slowing hot scanner paths | [doc 04 §3.1](../../../docs/04-modules.md) |
| Some write path bypasses audit entirely | — |
